solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Assembling at last (8)

blocks.note: putting something together roughly, from odds and ends
a last is the foot-shaped block a shoemaker works on

annotation.surface: Someone finally getting a thing put together.
annotation.walkthrough: 'At last' reads as 'finally', but here the last is the shoemaker's wooden foot, so working at the last is cobbling.
annotation.definitionFit: To cobble together is to assemble clumsily, and a cobbler mending shoes works at a last, so both senses meet.

entries.clue: Shuffled, the cards got harder (8)

annotation.definitionNote: 'got harder' is an intransitive past tense; STARCHED is the past tense of a transitive verb, 'made stiff'

indicatorNotes.Shuffled: shuffling cards mixes them, so the letters of THE CARDS are mixed

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

annotation.surface: A card game where the shuffled deck somehow makes play tougher.
annotation.walkthrough: The indicator comes straight from the surface: cards are exactly the thing one shuffles.
annotation.definitionFit: Starch stiffens fabric, so starched collars have been made harder.

entries.clue: Whenever dynamite fails to start exploding (7)

indicatorNotes.fails to start: the word loses its starting letter
indicatorNotes.exploding: what explodes is blown apart, so its letters are scattered

blocks.note: DYNAMITE without its first letter D

annotation.surface: A grumble that the dynamite never goes off when it should.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fails to start' looks like part of the dud-explosive story, but it is an instruction to drop the D.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Anytime' means at whatever time, the same as 'whenever'.

entries.clue: Cover article deleted too (6)

indicatorNotes.deleted: the article is taken out of the word for 'cover'

blocks.note: an overlay covers something
the indefinite article, removed from OVERLAY

annotation.surface: A magazine editor cutting a cover story along with something else.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Article' looks like a magazine piece; in crosswords it usually means A, AN or THE.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Overly' and 'too' both mean excessively, as in overly long or too long.

entries.clue: Incite first of riders to abandon foot support (4,2)

indicatorNotes.first of: take only the first letter of the next word
indicatorNotes.to abandon: that letter leaves the word it was in

blocks.note: a rider's foot rests in a stirrup
R, removed from STIRRUP

annotation.surface: A rider urged to kick their feet free of the stirrups.
annotation.walkthrough: Taking one R out of STIRRUP leaves STIRUP, split 4,2 as STIR UP; the riders and the foot support share one horse-riding picture.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: stirring a pot agitates it, and stirring people up agitates them into action, which is inciting them.

entries.clue: One undertaking crossing at sea? (8,5)

blocks.note: reads as a traveller setting out on a voyage; the setter means someone putting a cross on a ballot paper
reads as out on the water; the setter means undecided, all at sea over the choice, and the question mark flags the pun

annotation.surface: Someone making a voyage across the sea.
annotation.walkthrough: The crossing is the X marked on a ballot, and 'at sea' means undecided: a floating voter is still making up their mind as they vote.
annotation.definitionFit: A floating voter, tied to no party, still has to mark a cross on the ballot while all at sea over the choice.

entries.clue: Thief chatters about bent lines getting sewn up (7,6)

indicatorNotes.about: the letters are turned about into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 13 letters

annotation.surface: A thief talking about crooked lines that got stitched up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bent' and 'sewn up' read like thieves' slang for crooked and caught, but 'bent lines' describes the zigzag of the stitch.
annotation.definitionFit: Feather stitch is an embroidery stitch sewn in a zigzag of slanting lines.

entries.clue: Shallow jar and cups Enid smashed (6-7)

indicatorNotes.smashed: broken to pieces, so ENID's letters are rearranged

blocks.note: to jar someone is to rattle them
a bra is made of cups
ENID rearranged

annotation.surface: Enid breaking a shallow jar and some cups.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shallow' seems to describe the jar, but it is the definition; 'jar' is a verb here.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone rattle-brained is scatty and empty-headed, so shallow.

entries.clue: Boxer’s babble? (6)

blocks.note: one who jabs, throwing short straight punches
rapid, unintelligible chatter

annotation.surface: The punch-drunk ramblings of a boxer.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue looks like one idea, a boxer's talk, but the 's is 'is': a boxer is one who jabs, and babble is the second sense.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: -ER added to 'jab' makes a puncher, and jabber as a word of its own is fast meaningless talk, which is babble.

entries.clue: Salt, sailor’s said individual characteristic (8)

indicatorNotes.said: spoken, so the word is written as it sounds

blocks.note: tar is an old word for a sailor
a trait is an individual characteristic, pronounced 'trate'

annotation.surface: An old salt, and the peculiar things sailors are said to have.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Salt' looks like a sailor, which the surface supports, but it is the chemistry definition; the sailor is TAR.
annotation.definitionFit: A tartrate is a salt of tartaric acid, as in cream of tartar.

entries.clue: Greek character’s seen in clubhouse before one (3)

indicatorNotes.before: 'before' means earlier in order, so the clubhouse letters come ahead of the one when the word is read

blocks.note: the standard dictionary abbreviation, first and middle letters of the compound
Roman numeral one

annotation.surface: A notable Greek spotted at a golf clubhouse.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Character' looks like a person, but it is a letter of the Greek alphabet.
annotation.definitionFit: Chi, written X, is the twenty-second letter of the Greek alphabet.

entries.clue: Believer may accept his eminence as Arab leader (6)

indicatorNotes.may accept: the believer takes the other word inside

blocks.note: a follower of Sikhism
HE, His Eminence, a cardinal's title, goes inside SIKH

annotation.surface: A believer honouring a cardinal as leader of the Arabs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'His eminence' sounds like a person to respect, but it is only the abbreviation HE.
annotation.definitionFit: A sheikh is the chief of an Arab tribe or family.

entries.clue: My appeal’s thrown out by plant (3,5)

indicatorNotes.thrown out: tossed about, so the letters land in a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

annotation.surface: A legal appeal dismissed by a manufacturing plant's management.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a factory that has thrown out an appeal; it is the botanical definition.
annotation.definitionFit: The mayapple is a North American woodland plant with an apple-like fruit.

entries.clue: Woman showing force no resistance (3)

indicatorNotes.no: the R is taken away, leaving the word with no resistance

blocks.note: an army is a military force
R is the symbol for electrical resistance, removed from ARMY

annotation.surface: A woman standing firm and yielding nothing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Force' reads as strength; it is a body of troops.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: crosswords often clue a first name by the kind of person who bears it, and Amy is a girl's name.

entries.clue: Troops ordered to accept gear (7)

indicatorNotes.to accept: the first word takes the second inside

blocks.note: bade is the past tense of bid, to order
rig means equipment or outfit; it goes inside BADE

annotation.surface: Soldiers told to take delivery of their kit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' looks like an anagram indicator, but it is BADE.
annotation.definitionFit: A brigade is a military unit of several battalions, a body of troops.

entries.clue: A Michigan buddy (3)

blocks.note: used as it stands
MI is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Michigan

annotation.surface: A pal from Michigan.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer is a French word that English speakers know from 'mon ami'.
annotation.definitionFit: A foreign word used in English: the French for friend, which matches the American slang 'buddy'.

entries.clue: One regularly complaining about lines may get by after qualification (7)

indicatorNotes.after: 'after' means following in sequence, so BY is written following the qualification

blocks.note: c, circa, is Latin for about
RY, railway, is a set of lines
Bachelor of Arts, a degree
used as it stands

annotation.surface: A moaner grumbling about getting by on paper qualifications alone.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lines' feels like an actor's script or writing; it is railway lines. 'By' is taken literally.
annotation.definitionFit: A crybaby is someone who whines and complains constantly.

entries.clue: Nimble Rosy may be on top in this district! (3-5)

indicatorNotes.on top: in a down entry, RED goes above LIGHT

blocks.note: rosy is a red colour
light on one's feet means nimble

annotation.surface: A girl called Rosy, quick on her feet, coming out on top somewhere.
annotation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark flags the innuendo: in a red-light district someone may well be on top. Rosy looks like a name but is just RED.
annotation.definitionFit: A red-light district is an area of brothels and sex work, and the clue's suggestive 'on top' fits that.

entries.clue: Boastful talk envelopes associate supporter (8)

indicatorNotes.envelopes: wraps round the other letter like an envelope

blocks.note: bluster is loud, empty boasting
A is a standard abbreviation for associate; it goes inside BLUSTER

annotation.surface: A braggart wrapping a friend or backer in his boasts.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Supporter' seems to be a person; it is a post holding up a rail.
annotation.definitionFit: A baluster is one of the short pillars supporting a handrail or parapet.

entries.clue: Dreary old convict gets bird (7)

blocks.note: a grey day is a dreary one
an old lag is a long-term or repeat prisoner

annotation.surface: A dull ex-prisoner is given a bird, perhaps a prison sentence.
annotation.walkthrough: In British slang 'bird' means a prison term, which the convict surface exploits; here it is a real bird.
annotation.definitionFit: The greylag is a large grey goose, ancestor of most farmyard geese.

entries.clue: It’s a more flourishing spray (8)

indicatorNotes.flourishing: flourished, waved about, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

annotation.surface: A spray of flowers that blooms more lavishly than others.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as a gardener's remark; 'spray' is the device for fine mist.
annotation.definitionFit: An atomiser turns liquid into a fine spray, as with perfume.

entries.clue: Frenchman will get bulk of fruit tomorrow (6)

indicatorNotes.bulk of: most of the word, dropping its last letter

blocks.note: M, monsieur, is the French title for a man
ANANAS, the pineapple, without its last S

annotation.surface: A Frenchman promised most of the fruit order by tomorrow.
annotation.walkthrough: Ananas is the pineapple, the word for it in French and in many other languages.
annotation.definitionFit: A Spanish word borrowed into English, used both literally and for some vague later time, the put-it-off attitude.

entries.clue: Old scholar found stall in corner (6)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' means placed within, so the stall is put inside the corner's letters

blocks.note: the south-east corner, as of England
a crib is an animal's stall or manger

annotation.surface: An old academic discovered setting up a stall in a corner.
annotation.walkthrough: The corner is a compass corner, SE.
annotation.definitionFit: Among the ancient Jews a scribe was a scholar and teacher of the Law.

entries.clue: As many as there are in sad disarray in the city (6)

indicatorNotes.in: ALL goes inside the rearranged SAD
indicatorNotes.disarray: in disarray, so the letters of SAD are jumbled

blocks.note: all of them
SAD rearranged, split D…AS around ALL

annotation.surface: A gloomy, chaotic crowd in the city.
annotation.walkthrough: 'As many as there are' is a roundabout way to say ALL.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Texas city of oil money and the old TV soap stands for the whole class of cities.

entries.clue: Odd characters left real ale measure (3)

indicatorNotes.Odd characters left: the odd-numbered letters have left, so the even ones stay

blocks.note: REAL ALE with its 1st, 3rd, 5th and 7th letters gone

annotation.surface: A pub pint where the odd drinkers have left the real ale.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like the direction or L, but it means departed: the odd letters go, not stay.
annotation.definitionFit: An ell is an old measure of length, about 45 inches.

entries.clue: Swimmer mean about artist (8)

indicatorNotes.about: 'about' means around, so the word for mean is placed around the artist

blocks.note: stingy means miserly
RA, Royal Academician, goes inside STINGY

annotation.surface: A tight-fisted swimmer grumbling about an artist.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like average or intend; it is miserly.
annotation.definitionFit: A stingray is a flat fish, a creature that swims.

entries.clue: Matching like crockery perhaps being washed up, we hear (2,4)

indicatorNotes.we hear: what is heard, so the spelling follows the sound

blocks.clueFragment: like crockery perhaps being washed up
blocks.note: dishes being washed up sit in the sink

annotation.surface: A matching set of plates in the washing-up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Washed up' is British for washing the dishes, and crockery in the sink sounds just like in sync.
annotation.definitionFit: Two things in sync are synchronised, matching each other.

entries.clue: Suspend heady brat at loggerheads precariously placed (4,2,1,6)

annotation.definitionNote: 'precariously placed' is an adjective phrase; HANG BY A THREAD is a verb phrase meaning to be precariously placed

indicatorNotes.at loggerheads: at odds, so the letters are set against each other in a new order

blocks.note: to hang is to suspend
HEADY BRAT rearranged

annotation.surface: Hanging a hot-headed brat who is quarrelling with everyone.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like a punishment; the anagram of HEADY BRAT is where the answer's second half comes from.
annotation.definitionFit: Something hanging by a thread is in a precarious position.
